svg.title: Critical friend: journey through the playbook
svg.desc: Seven stops on one assignment, from being asked to saying what you assured.

div.b: Critical friend: journey through the playbook

div.span: Seven stops on one assignment, from being asked to saying what you assured.

div.b: 1. You have been asked to be a critical friend
2. How far from the work do I have to sit?
6. Has the uncertainty been handled honestly?

div.span:
The critical friend
What you are confirming

div.div: You give independent advice. You are not delivering the analysis.
The separation follows the level, from a colleague to external review.
Review the plan. Confirm the approach and assurance level are right.
Run the checks the level asks for, and the levels inside it.
You shall review the analyst's assurance and report errors and improvements back.
Check assumptions are traceable, and uncertainty quantified where the method allows.
State the assurance: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented.

div.span: The evidence trail, read on its own

div.div: Nothing recorded yet.
Your name on the design and plan, before work starts.
A reviewed assurance plan, and your time in the schedule.
Your entries in the quality assurance log.
Your findings, and the analyst's response to each one.
A recorded view on whether uncertainty is handled adequately.
The quality assurance statement, or your part of it.

div.span: What the playbook warns about here

div.div: You and the analyst shall be independent in all cases.
Found afterwards, you review what was produced. Named beforehand, you shape it.
A plan with no time in the schedule is only intent.
The log records which checks, when, and what you found.
Reporting them is yours. Acting on them is the analyst's.
Limitations in the output rather than only in an annex.

div.span: Stop 7 loops back to stop 2. What you report back is what the next piece of work avoids.

Open alongside, at any stop. R8 for what binds the work in front of you. Deciding your assurance level to check the level is right, because assuring to the wrong level is a finding in itself. R2 for the checklist and the log.
NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Kainos Software Limited, SOW-DOC053.
